 TV Talk: Final ‘Mayor of Kingstown’ episodes stream in January
 By Rob Owen 3 Min Read

 | 4 days ago

 Jeremy Renner stars as Mike McLusky in “Mayor of Kingstown” season 5, streaming on Paramount+ in January 2027. (Courtesy Jeremy Parsons/Paramount+) 
 Derek Webster as Stevie, Hugh Dillon as Ian and Jeremy Renner as Mike McLusky in “Mayor of Kingstown” season 5, streaming on Paramount+ in January 2027. (Courtesy Jeremy Parsons/Paramount+) 
 Tobi Bamtefa as Deverin “Bunny” Washington and Jeremy Renner as Mike McLusky in “Mayor of Kingstown” season 5, streaming on Paramount+ in January 2027. (Courtesy Jeremy Parsons/Paramount+) 
 Clark Backo, Carrie-Anne Moss, Hudson Williams and Noah Reid star in “Yaga” (Courtesy AMC+) 
 Hudson Williams stars in “Yaga.” (Courtesy AMC+) 
 Hudson Williams and Carrie-Anne Moss star in “Yaga.” (Courtesy AMC+) 
 After wrapping production in Pittsburgh on its fifth and final season in early summer, “Mayor of Kingstown” will return to Paramount+ with new episodes on Jan. 15.
 The show’s eight-episode swan song brings back stars Jeremy Renner, Edie Falco, Laura Benanti, Hugh Dillon, Taylor Handley, Tobi Bamtefa, Derek Webster, Necar Zadegan, Nichole Galicia and Lennie James. David Morse, who starred in Pittsburgh-filmed “Outsiders,” joins the cast.
 The final season’s logline: “In the wake of Tracy’s murder and the vengeance visited upon Callahan by Mike (Renner) and Kyle (Handley), FBI agent Russell Hardy (Morse) arrives in Kingstown searching for the ‘fugitive’ Callahan. A true lawman, Agent Hardy threatens to unearth all of Mike’s sins and secrets and disrupt Kingstown’s tenuous balance of power.”
 ‘Yaga’ 
 Hudson Williams went from unknown to very much known thanks to last year’s surprise pop culture hit “Heated Rivalry,” and now he’s back — times two! — in a new Canadian import, comedic thriller “Yaga,” streaming its first two (of eight) half-hour episodes Friday on AMC+.
 Noah Reid (“Outer Range”) plays a rumpled detective, Rapp, who partners with a small-town cop (Clark Backo, “Letterkenny”) to find missing billionaire heir Henry Park (Williams), who has a look-alike roommate, Logan (Williams, again).
 Created by Kat Sandler, the series is based on her play of the same name that was a reimagining of the Slavic folk tale of Baba Yaga, who’s either a terrifying ogress or a boundary-crossing mentor.
 In AMC+’s “Yaga,” Carrie-Anne Moss (“The Matrix”) plays a seductive university lecturer who Henry may have been obsessed with.
 Through its first three episodes, “Yaga” proves itself to be a pretty good yarn that mixes humor with hints of supernatural elements at play.
 Reid, a standout on “Schitt’s Creek,” is “Yaga’s” nominal lead character, a scruffy, rascally good guy who’s not so upstanding that he won’t try to bed some of the young women of the town he’s stuck in for his investigation.
 In early episodes, Williams’ role is small, but since the show is set up around finding his missing character, it seems likely Williams will get more to do deeper into the show’s run.
 Like the recent “Phony,” “Yaga” is another welcome mystery that sets up a seemingly impossible conundrum to be solved, and it’s not clear how the show will pull that off. That lack of predictability makes both series worth watching.
 Channel surfing 
 Getting out while the getting is good: After 43 years, CNN international anchor and correspondent Christiane Amanpour announced that next summer she’ll leave the network that was just acquired by Skydance and sure to go through a large round of job cuts now that CBS News and CNN are owned by the same company. … Nicolas Cage and Antonio Banderas will star in the fifth season of HBO’s “True Detective,” set to film in 2027. … Jon Stewart signed a two-year extension to continue hosting Comedy Central’s “The Daily Show” one night per week through 2028. … Apple TV renewed “Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed” for a second season. … Super Bowl LXI will get an animated “Star Wars Funday Football” alternative broadcast on Disney+ and cable’s Disney XD.
